tables.name: customers
tables.business_purpose: Master record for every customer account (company) that has ever held a subscription, including accounts acquired before the reporting window.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Stable unique customer identifier.
columns.expected_values: Format CUST-000001; assigned in signup order.
columns.business_meaning: Join key used across all customer-level tables.

columns.name: company_name
columns.description: Legal name of the customer company (synthetic).
columns.expected_values: Unique, synthetic company names with a country-specific legal suffix.
columns.business_meaning: Human-readable account name for reporting.

columns.name: country
columns.description: Country of the customer's billing entity.
columns.business_meaning: Geographic market; Singapore is the headquarters market.

columns.name: region
columns.description: Sales region derived from country.
columns.business_meaning: Territory used for sales coverage and regional P&L.

columns.name: industry
columns.description: Customer's primary industry.
columns.business_meaning: Vertical used for segmentation and marketing targeting.

columns.name: company_size
columns.description: Employee-count band of the customer company.
columns.business_meaning: Determines segment: 1-200 SMB, 201-1000 Mid-Market, 1001+ Enterprise.

columns.name: segment
columns.description: Commercial segment derived from company size.
columns.business_meaning: Primary segmentation for pricing, sales motion and reporting.

columns.name: acquisition_channel
columns.description: Channel that sourced the customer.
columns.business_meaning: Marketing channels match marketing_campaigns.channel; 'Outbound Sales' and 'Referral' have no campaign spend.

columns.name: signup_date
columns.description: Date the first subscription started.
columns.business_meaning: Start of the customer relationship; basis for cohorts and tenure.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Account status as of the dataset end date.
columns.business_meaning: 'churned' means no active subscription at the dataset end date.

tables.name: subscriptions
tables.business_purpose: Versioned subscription history. A new record starts whenever a customer's contracted MRR changes (expansion or contraction); the prior record is closed as 'superseded'. Churn closes the final record with status 'churned'.
tables.grain: One row per customer subscription period with constant plan, seats and MRR.

columns.name: subscription_id
columns.description: Unique subscription record identifier.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Customer holding the subscription.

columns.name: plan
columns.description: Subscription plan (price tier).
columns.business_meaning: Starter < Growth < Professional < Enterprise in price and features.

columns.name: seats
columns.description: Number of licensed user seats.
columns.business_meaning: Main pricing driver: MRR is approximately seats x plan price per seat.

columns.name: monthly_recurring_revenue
columns.description: Contracted MRR in SGD for this subscription period.
columns.business_meaning: Recurring revenue while this record is in force.

columns.name: start_date
columns.description: First day this subscription record is in force.

columns.name: end_date
columns.description: Last day this subscription record is in force; NULL while active.
columns.business_meaning: For churned records this is the last day of service.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Record status as of the dataset end date.
columns.business_meaning: 'active' = in force; 'superseded' = replaced by a later record for the same customer (expansion/contraction); 'churned' = customer cancelled.

columns.name: change_type
columns.description: How this record began.
columns.business_meaning: 'new' = first subscription; 'expansion' / 'contraction' = MRR increased / decreased versus previous_mrr.

columns.name: previous_mrr
columns.description: Customer MRR immediately before this record started (0 for new customers).
columns.business_meaning: MRR movement at start = monthly_recurring_revenue - previous_mrr.

columns.name: current_mrr
columns.description: MRR contributed by this record as of the dataset end date.
columns.business_meaning: SUM(current_mrr) gives total MRR at the dataset end date.

tables.name: usage_events
tables.business_purpose: Weekly product-usage telemetry per customer account.
tables.grain: One row per customer per week (weeks start on Monday). A week is recorded when the customer was subscribed for at least 4 of its 7 days.

columns.name: event_id
columns.description: Unique usage record identifier.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Customer account.

columns.name: event_date
columns.description: Monday that starts the usage week.
columns.business_meaning: Weekly time key for usage trend analysis.

columns.name: active_users
columns.description: Distinct users active during the week (weekly active users).
columns.business_meaning: Core engagement measure; declining values signal disengagement.

columns.name: sessions
columns.description: Number of user sessions during the week.

columns.name: api_calls
columns.description: API calls made during the week.
columns.expected_values: >= 0; always 0 on the Starter plan (no API access).
columns.business_meaning: Drives usage (overage) revenue above the plan's included quota.

columns.name: feature_usage
columns.description: Number of distinct product features used during the week.
columns.expected_values: 0 to 12 (bounded by the features available on the plan).
columns.business_meaning: Breadth of adoption; broader usage indicates deeper product fit.

tables.name: sales_opportunities
tables.business_purpose: CRM opportunities for sales-assisted deals: new business (prospects and won customers) and expansion of existing accounts.

columns.name: opportunity_id
columns.description: Unique opportunity identifier.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Customer account; NULL for new-business prospects that have not become customers.
columns.business_meaning: Populated for all won and expansion opportunities.

columns.name: sales_rep
columns.description: Sales representative who owns the opportunity (synthetic name).
columns.business_meaning: Owner used for rep-level performance analysis.

columns.name: opportunity_type
columns.description: Deal type.

columns.name: segment
columns.description: Segment of the prospect or customer.

columns.name: region
columns.description: Sales region (rep territory).

columns.name: created_date
columns.description: Date the opportunity was created.

columns.name: close_date
columns.description: Date the opportunity was won or lost; NULL while open.

columns.name: stage
columns.description: Current stage (final stage for closed opportunities).
columns.business_meaning: Lead -> Qualified -> Proposal -> Negotiation -> Won; Lost can occur at any stage.

columns.name: furthest_stage
columns.description: Furthest funnel stage reached (for lost deals: the stage at which the deal was lost).
columns.business_meaning: Enables stage-to-stage conversion and drop-off analysis.

columns.name: deal_value
columns.description: Annual contract value (SGD) of the opportunity.
columns.expected_values: > 0. For won deals = 12 x MRR added.

columns.name: probability
columns.description: CRM win probability for the current stage.
columns.expected_values: Lead 0.10, Qualified 0.25, Proposal 0.50, Negotiation 0.75, Won 1.00, Lost 0.00.
columns.business_meaning: Used to weight open pipeline.

tables.name: support_tickets
tables.business_purpose: Customer support tickets with priority, category, resolution and sentiment.

columns.name: ticket_id
columns.description: Unique ticket identifier.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Customer that raised the ticket.

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: When the ticket was opened.

columns.name: resolved_at
columns.description: When the ticket was resolved; NULL if still open at the dataset end.

columns.name: priority
columns.description: Ticket priority.

columns.name: category
columns.description: Ticket category.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Ticket status at the dataset end date.

columns.name: resolution_time
columns.description: Hours from creation to resolution; NULL while open.
columns.business_meaning: Service-level measure; long resolution times hurt customer experience.

columns.name: sentiment
columns.description: Customer sentiment classified from the ticket conversation.

tables.name: marketing_campaigns
tables.business_purpose: Weekly marketing campaign performance: spend and funnel metrics.
tables.grain: One row per campaign per week (weeks start on Monday).

columns.name: campaign_id
columns.description: Campaign identifier.

columns.name: campaign_name
columns.description: Descriptive campaign name (channel | theme | quarter).

columns.name: channel
columns.description: Marketing channel.

columns.name: date
columns.description: Monday that starts the reporting week.

columns.name: spend
columns.description: Media / programme spend in SGD for the week.

columns.name: impressions
columns.description: Ad impressions, sends or content views.

columns.name: clicks
columns.description: Clicks or engaged visits.

columns.name: leads
columns.description: Marketing-qualified leads generated.

columns.name: conversions
columns.description: Leads that became paying customers during the week.
columns.business_meaning: Each conversion corresponds to one customer with acquisition_channel = channel and a signup_date in the same week.

tables.name: daily_revenue
tables.business_purpose: Daily recognised revenue per customer. Subscription revenue is recognised daily as MRR x 12 / 365; usage revenue is API overage above the plan quota, recognised evenly across the customer's active days in the month.
tables.grain: One row per customer per day per revenue type.

columns.name: date
columns.description: Revenue recognition date.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Customer account.

columns.name: region
columns.description: Customer region (denormalised for reporting).

columns.name: segment
columns.description: Customer segment (denormalised).

columns.name: plan
columns.description: Plan in force on this date.

columns.name: revenue_type
columns.description: Revenue stream.

columns.name: revenue
columns.description: Revenue recognised on this date in SGD.
columns.business_meaning: SUM over a period gives recognised revenue for that period.

tables.name: product_features
tables.business_purpose: Daily feature-level adoption across the whole customer base.
tables.grain: One row per feature per day, from the feature's launch date onwards.

columns.name: feature_id
columns.description: Feature identifier.

columns.name: feature_name
columns.description: Feature name.

columns.name: date
columns.description: Calendar date.

columns.name: active_users
columns.description: Users who used the feature on this date.

columns.name: adoption_rate
columns.description: Share of the platform's daily active users who used the feature.
columns.business_meaning: Feature penetration; rising values indicate successful adoption.

views.name: v_monthly_revenue
views.description: Recognised revenue by calendar month, region, segment, plan and revenue type.

views.name: v_monthly_mrr
views.description: Month-end MRR snapshot per customer: subscriptions in force on the last day of each month in the reporting window.

views.name: v_subscription_events
views.description: Subscription movements derived from the versioned subscriptions table: new, expansion, contraction (at record start) and churn (at the last day of service).

views.name: v_campaign_summary
views.description: Campaign-level totals of spend and funnel volumes across all active weeks.
